title: Exposure to hostile or degrading online content is concentrated among younger EU users and differs by gender and target
source_unit: Eurostat 2025 EU survey on ICT usage by households and individuals, published 18 June 2026

observations.period: 2025; exposure to hostile or degrading online content by age

denominator.unit: EU internet users aged 16-74 who encountered online content during the reference period; comparative percentage frame

hostile_content_age_16_24.unit: percent of internet users ages 16-24 encountering hostile or degrading content directed at groups or individuals

mechanism.value: The platform environment is not experienced evenly: younger users encounter more hostile or degrading content, making exposure, moderation, identity safety, and exit conditions part of digital cultural and civic infrastructure

observations.method: Eurostat summary of the 2025 EU survey on ICT usage by households and individuals; hostile or degrading content includes messages, comments, photos, memes, videos, and other material directed at specific groups or individuals.
observations.uncertainty: Exposure can be to content directed at the respondent or at other people; the indicator does not measure frequency, severity, direct victimization, reporting, platform response, mental-health effects, political behavior, or causal harm.
observations.subgroup: EU internet users aged 16-74 by age group.
observations.counterinterpretation: Younger users may spend more time online or use different services, increasing exposure opportunity; lower exposure among older users does not imply a safer or more inclusive digital experience.

observations.period: 2025; hostile or degrading online content among internet users ages 16-24 by gender and content target

denominator.unit: EU internet users ages 16-24; comparative percentage frame

young_women_any_hostile_content.unit: percent of young female internet users reporting exposure

young_men_any_hostile_content.unit: percent of young male internet users reporting exposure

young_political_social_views_women_men.unit: percent of young women versus young men encountering hostile content about political or social views

young_racial_ethnic_origin_women_men.unit: percent of young women versus young men encountering hostile content about racial or ethnic origin

largest_gender_gaps.value: sexual orientation 37.8% versus 32.6%; sex 30.9% versus 24.9%; disability 23.0% versus 19.3%

mechanism.value: Young women report higher exposure overall and across several identity targets, indicating that digital participation may carry unequal recognition, safety, and moderation burdens even within the same age cohort

observations.method: Eurostat cross-tabulation of 2025 ICT-use survey responses for internet users ages 16-24, disaggregated by gender and hostile-content target.
observations.uncertainty: The published comparison is descriptive and does not establish differential time online, platform mix, reporting behavior, message severity, perpetrator identity, moderator action, or downstream wellbeing and participation outcomes.
observations.subgroup: EU internet users ages 16-24, comparing young women and young men across content targets.
observations.counterinterpretation: Gender differences may reflect different exposure opportunities, recognition or reporting thresholds, platform use, or social context; exposure is not equivalent to direct victimization or measured harm.

boundary: This record adds an official EU digital-exposure and identity-safety layer. It does not establish direct victimization, severity, platform causality, moderation effectiveness, mental-health outcomes, political behavior, cultural belonging, or consumer welfare.
